dedupe_keys.name: simulated reverse clock auctions for the fcc incentive auction economic outcomes with simulated bidder behaviour newman leyton brown milgrom and segal

description: This paper investigates the economic outcomes of a model of the FCC's reverse auction, the part of the 2016 to 2017 incentive auction in which the FCC bought spectrum from TV broadcasters and repacked the remaining stations into fewer channels. The forward auction resold the cleared spectrum to mobile carriers for $19.8 billion. In simulations with simulated bidder behaviour, and treating the reverse auction in isolation, the reverse clock auction achieves very efficient solutions, the FCC's scoring rule greatly reduces total payments to broadcasters at the cost of some efficiency, and a poor feasibility checker can have grave consequences for both cost and efficiency. Repacking is not always possible because nearby channels interfere. Producer: Newman, Leyton-Brown, Milgrom and Segal; the PDF is dated October 2018, arXiv v1 June 2017. Coverage: United States television stations. Access: free arXiv PDF; the abstract and introduction were read, code and data were not seen. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: it studies the reverse auction in isolation, and the bidder behaviour is simulated. Simulation uses: the model links broadcast station repacking constraints to economic outcomes for spectrum reallocation studies. Related record: the FCC incentive auction economics paper (model-fcc-incentive-auction-economics-computer-science-spectrum-reallocation).
